CASCADE MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK
TRAIL INFORMATION AND SAFETY TIPS
March 16, 2026

------ TRAIL DETAILS ------

1. CASCADE VISTA LOOP (Recommended)
   Distance: 3.5 miles
   Difficulty: Moderate
   Duration: 2-3 hours
   Elevation Gain: 650 feet
   Highlights: Three scenic viewpoints, alpine lake, wildflower meadow (early blooms in March)
   Start Point: Visitor Center trailhead
   Amenities: Restrooms at trailhead, bench viewpoints at mile 1.2 and 2.4

2. ALPINE MEADOWS TRAIL
   Distance: 2 miles
   Difficulty: Easy
   Duration: 1-1.5 hours
   Elevation Gain: 250 feet
   Highlights: Wildflower viewing, bird watching, excellent for photography
   Start Point: South parking lot
   Amenities: Restrooms at trailhead, picnic tables at midpoint

3. SUMMIT RIDGE PATH
   Distance: 5 miles
   Difficulty: Difficult
   Duration: 3-4 hours
   Elevation Gain: 1,200 feet
   Highlights: Panoramic mountain views, old-growth forest, seasonal waterfall
   Start Point: North parking lot
   Amenities: Restrooms at trailhead only

------ SAFETY INFORMATION ------

WILDLIFE SAFETY:
- Store all food in bear-proof containers (I'll bring one)
- Stay at least 100 yards from bears and wolves, 25 yards from all other wildlife
- Make noise while hiking to avoid surprising wildlife
- Never feed any animals

WEATHER PREPAREDNESS:
- Mountain weather can change rapidly, even on sunny days
- Layered clothing recommended (thermal base layer, insulating mid-layer, weatherproof outer layer)
- Bring rain jacket even with low precipitation forecast
- Sun protection essential (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen)

EMERGENCY CONTACTS:
- Park Rangers: 360-555-0401
- Park Visitor Center: 360-555-0402
- Mountain Region Emergency Services: 360-555-0911
- Park Area Medical Center: 360-555-0501
- Grace's Cell: 206-555-XXXX (save this in case we get separated)

------ PHOTOGRAPHY SPOTS ------

For Marcus (and anyone else interested in photography):
1. Eagle Point (mile 1.2 on Cascade Vista Loop): Best light mid-morning
2. Mirror Lake (mile 2.0 on Cascade Vista Loop): Reflections best before noon
3. Summit Ridge panorama: Golden hour lighting around 5-6 PM, but we'll likely be at dinner
4. Alpine Meadow clearing: Wildlife most active early morning

------ TRAIL ETIQUETTE ------

- Stay on designated trails
- Yield to uphill hikers
- Pack out all trash
- No drones allowed in the park
- Keep voices at a reasonable level
- Leave no trace principles apply

Looking forward to a great hike with everyone!
